title: Fair outputs, Biased Internals: Causal Potency and Asymmetry of Latent Bias in LLMs for High-Stakes Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2605.15217v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Instruction-tuned language models exhibit behavioural fairness in high-stakes decisions while retaining biased associations in their internal representations. However, whether these suppressed representations can affect model outputs - and whether such causal potency is symmetric across demographic groups - remains unknown. We investigate the use of open-weight models for mortgage underwriting using matched applications that differ only in racially-associated names and reveal a critical disconnect: models show no output-level bias, yet retain and amplify demographic representations across model layers. Through activation steering and novel cross-layer interventions, we demonstrate that this suppressed information is decision-relevant: when reinjected at critical layers, it produces near-complete decision reversals. translated_title: 公平的输出，有偏见的内部：大语言模型在高风险决策中潜在偏见的因果效力与不对称性
translated_abstract: 经过指令微调的语言模型在高风险决策中表现出行为层面的公平性，同时其内部表征中仍保留着有偏见的关联。然而，这些被抑制的表征是否能够影响模型输出——以及这种因果效力是否在不同人口群体之间对称——仍然未知。我们使用仅在种族相关姓名上不同的匹配申请，研究了开源权重模型在抵押贷款承保中的应用，并揭示了一个关键的脱节现象：模型在输出层面没有表现出偏见，但在模型各层中却保留并放大了人口统计表征。通过激活引导和新型跨层干预方法，我们证明这些被抑制的信息与决策相关：当在关键层重新注入时，会产生近乎完全的决策逆转。至关重要的是，这种潜在偏见是不对称的——引导干预仅在一个人口统计方向上影响决策。
tldr: 该研究发现大语言模型在高风险抵押贷款决策中虽然输出公平，但其内部各层仍保留并放大的种族偏见表征具有因果效力，重新注入可导致决策近乎完全逆转，且这种潜在偏见在不同人口群体间是不对称的。
en_tdlr: LLMs exhibit fair outputs in high-stakes mortgage underwriting while internally retaining and amplifying racially-biased representations that are causally potent—reinjecting them at critical layers causes near-complete decision reversals—and this latent bias is asymmetric across demographic groups.
